title: What is a competency framework?
description: A competency framework defines the knowledge, skills and behaviors each role needs and the standard expected. What it contains and how it is used.
shortAnswer: A competency framework is a structured description of the knowledge, skills and behaviors an organization expects in each role, with the standard of performance that counts as competent. It gives training, assessment, recruitment and workforce planning a single reference point, so every learning activity and every assessment decision can be traced back to a defined requirement rather than to an individual trainer's judgment.
keyTakeaways: A competency framework lists competencies, groups them, and states the performance standard or proficiency level required for each role.

National vocational systems use precise definitions: Australia's, for example, defines competency as the consistent application of knowledge and skill to the standard of performance required in the workplace.
Nationally endorsed occupational standards, such as the units of competency on training.gov.au, are a ready source of wording and evidence requirements for internal frameworks.
A framework is only useful when it drives assessment: each competency needs observable evidence and a named way of checking it.

sections.heading: What does a competency framework contain?

blocks.text: A competency framework contains a list of competencies, a definition of each, the behaviors or evidence that show it, and the level required for each role. Most frameworks also group competencies into clusters (technical, regulatory, interpersonal, leadership) so they can be reused across job families.

National vocational systems often use a precise definition. For example, in Australia's vocational education and training (VET) system, the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations (DEWR) [Training Package Organizing Framework](https://www.dewr.gov.au/download/16680/training-package-organising-framework-effective-1-july-2025/39042/training-package-organising-framework/pdf), in effect from 1 July 2025, states that "Competency is defined as the consistent application of knowledge and skill to the standard of performance required in the workplace." The same document adds that competency covers performing functions, responding to contingencies and dealing with workplace responsibilities, including working with others.

blocks.text: Competency frameworks sit underneath most structured workforce training, from national vocational systems to internal frameworks in banks, hospitals, mines and government agencies. In the VET system described above, training packages specify competencies as units of competency, which are published on [training.gov.au](https://training.gov.au), the national register.

Under the Training Package Organizing Framework, a unit of competency sets out elements and performance criteria (or, in the newer template, the application of skills and knowledge), plus assessment requirements covering performance evidence, knowledge evidence and assessment conditions. Organizations building an internal framework often borrow this structure because it already separates what someone must do from what they must know.

National skills classifications also change. For example, Jobs and Skills Australia decommissioned the [Australian Skills Classification](https://www.jobsandskills.gov.au/data/australian-skills-classification) in December 2023 and is developing a [National Skills Taxonomy](https://www.jobsandskills.gov.au/data/national-skills-taxonomy) intended as a common language for skills across education and work. Internal frameworks that referenced the old classification should record that dependency and review it once the new taxonomy is published.

sections.heading: How is a competency framework different from a skills matrix or a training matrix?

blocks.text: A competency framework defines what competence means; a [skills matrix](/glossary/skills-matrix) records who currently has it; a [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) records what training each role must complete. The framework is the reference the other two are built from.

items: **Competency framework vs skills framework:** a skills framework usually lists skills without behaviors or performance standards. See [competency framework vs skills framework](/compare/competency-framework-vs-skills-framework).

**Competency framework vs learning outcomes:** [learning outcomes](/glossary/learning-outcomes) describe what a learner can do at the end of a course; competencies describe what a worker must do in the role.
**Competency framework vs training needs analysis:** a [training needs analysis](/glossary/training-needs-analysis) compares current capability with the framework to find gaps.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry treats the competency framework as structured data rather than a document: each competency is linked to its source obligation, the concepts it depends on, and the assessment points that evidence it. That makes gaps and outdated requirements visible when a source changes.

faqs.q: Is a competency framework the same as a capability framework?
faqs.a: The terms are often used interchangeably. Some organizations use capability to mean broader potential, including behaviors and attributes, and competency to mean demonstrated performance against a standard. What matters is that the framework defines its terms, states the required level for each role, and explains how each item is assessed.

faqs.q: How many competencies should a framework have?
faqs.a: There is no set number. A framework should hold enough competencies to describe the work that carries risk or value, and few enough that each one is actually assessed. If a competency has no assessment method attached, it is usually a sign that it is too vague or that the framework has grown beyond what can be maintained.

faqs.q: Can an organization use nationally endorsed units of competency in its own framework?
faqs.a: Yes. Many organizations reference nationally endorsed units of competency for technical or safety critical tasks because the elements, performance criteria and assessment requirements are already written and industry endorsed. Issuing a nationally recognized statement of attainment for those units, however, can only be done by a Registered Training Organisation.

faqs.q: How often should a competency framework be reviewed?
faqs.a: Review it whenever a source it depends on changes, such as a regulation, standard, procedure or role design, and on a fixed cycle as a backstop. Recording the source and owner of each competency makes change driven review practical, because the affected competencies can be found quickly.

factCheck.claim: Training Package Organising Framework date of effect 1 July 2025 defines competency as the consistent application of knowledge and skill to the standard of performance required in the workplace

Units of competency use either the Application, Elements and Performance Criteria template or the Application of Skills and Knowledge template; assessment requirements include performance evidence, knowledge evidence and assessment conditions
The Australian Skills Classification was decommissioned by Jobs and Skills Australia in December 2023; JSA is developing a National Skills Taxonomy
